source_title: Inside Ian McKellen and Patrick Stewart’s Decades-Long Friendship - People.com
source_excerpt:
From starring in movies and plays to officiating weddings, McKellen and Stewart remained close until the latter’s recent death
Tommy McArdle is a Writer-Reporter on the Movies team at PEOPLE. He joined the brand in 2022.
Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86 on Oct. 28
His friendship with Sir Ian McKellen, one of many who shared emotional tributes to the late star, stretched back decades
Stewart and McKellen starred together in the X-Men films and onstage at the Royal Shakespeare Company, the West End and Broadway
Sir Ian McKellen and Sir Patrick Stewart were costars, collaborators and, most of all, friends.
Following the announcement on Thursday, Oct. 29, that Stewart died at age 86, many fans and followers of McKellen sent condolences via his social media accounts. The two X-Men costars have known each other since at least the 1970s when they were early-career stage actors at the Royal Shakespeare Company in their native England.
McKellen, 87, himself penned a moving tribute to his late friend. “He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love,” wrote the Lord of the Rings Oscar nominee.
“We first met as ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago but we weren’t in the same productions,” he continued. “My first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in ‘Star Trek’. ‘But Patrick think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to risk—getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?’. Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did.”
As for what Stewart thought of McKellen, he recalled being “frankly intimidated” when McKellen joined the theater company. “I had admired him from the start of his career,” Stewart said in a 2019 interview with The Guardian .
While continuing his work in British theater, Stewart became known for film and television, famously portraying Captain Picard in the Star Trek franchise. The actor-activist then played mutant Professor X, joining McKellen as Magneto on-screen in the 2000 superhero blockbuster X-Men and many of the franchise’s sequels.
It was on the set of those movies that their friendship was cemented. “It’s only in the last couple of decades that we’ve become like brothers. It was due to X-Men, in fact,” Stewart told The Guardian in 2022.
He said the two grew close as they visited each other’s adjoining trailers between takes. “It was the element that made me most grateful for X-Men: that it brought Ian into my life,” he said.
The two began taking their collaboration to the next level, starring in a 2009 West End production of Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot . Their friend Dame Judi Dench recalled in her new memoir Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It? (on bookshelves Nov. 3) that she and her costars in a neighboring production began spreading playful rumors about McKellen and Stewart: that they had bought a home, acquired a puppy and even adopted a baby together.
McKellen and Stewart were indeed not shy about sharing their affections, even sharing a public smooch on red carpets.
In 2013 they took Broadway by storm in not one but two acclaimed productions in repertory at New York City’s Cort Theatre. The two actors alternately played roles in Waiting for Godot and Harold Pinter’s No Man’s Land .
After the final curtain fell on Godot , McKellen famously wept that it was over.
“I recall vividly,” Stewart told CBS News at the time, laughing. “In fact, it’s on film. I had no idea it was going to come. But the curtain came down on our last performance, and he went into the wings and sat on some stone steps and sobbed, heartbroken that it was over.”
“Yes, I was heartbroken,” McKellen added. “And then we were going to say goodbye to each other. You were going off to do other things and I just felt I would never be as happy again.”

Also in 2013, McKellen officiated Stewart’s wedding with Sunny Ozell . They celebrated at a ceremony in Lake Tahoe, although Stewart later revealed that because McKellen’s marriage credentials weren’t valid in Nevada, the couple were officially wed by McKellen at a Mexican restaurant in Los Angeles.
McKellen and Stewart were each knighted by the late Queen Elizabeth II in 1991 and 2010, respectively. In the 2000s, they continued reprising their roles as Magneto and Professor X, and recently returned to the parts in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday .
Speaking about his favorite memories from the set of the Marvel movie, costar Anthony Mackie recently recalled to PEOPLE that seeing McKellen and Stewart together was a special treat. “They’ve been friends for like 60 years. They’ve known each other forever,” he said.
“Ian walks over to Patrick and he goes, ‘Hey, what’s up?’ They hug each other, and they just whisper quietly to each other. Everybody was standing there like, ‘What the hell are they saying?’ ” recalled Mackie, 48, with a laugh. “Everybody would just stand back and look in awe, the amazement of these two dudes together and knowing everything that they’ve seen and how much they’ve experienced in their careers and lives.”
Avengers: Doomsday star Simu Liu similarly raved about working with two “iconic” Marvel legends. “Getting to talk to them, getting to hang on set with them in between takes, it was the most starstruck I’ve ever been,” said Liu, 37.
Fans can see Stewart and McKellen together again in Avengers: Doomsday , in theaters Dec. 18.
Stewart, a father of two , is survived by Ozell.
